correctness.rationale: The equilibrium is deduced by two independent mean-occupancy equations and two patch-free-space identities, uniquely yielding the positive solution. Differentiation of the exact four-dimensional ODE gives a symmetric Jacobian commuting with simultaneous species/habitat swap. The two explicit 2×2 invariant blocks yield all four eigenvalues, and comparison of their off-diagonal magnitudes identifies the strictly dominant mode. A positive difference-of-squares factor establishes strict monotonicity for every r>1 and 0<delta<r. Taylor and boundary expansions give the sharp quadratic weak-heterogeneity and saturation limits. The separately runnable stdlib exact-rational checker tests 20 configurations; the quantified result rests on the algebra, not samples.

value.rationale: The minimal two-species/two-habitat setup isolates the mechanism of opposing habitat preference with no change in either species mean abundance or total habitat occupancy. The all-parameter exact recovery rate determines a measurable resilience scale absent from steady-state occupancy data; its sharp delta^{-2} near-neutral divergence reveals severely slow compositional recovery even when a unique strictly stable coexistence equilibrium exists. The strict monotonicity and finite limiting gap resolve a natural whole-interval question, not an arbitrary isolated parameter evaluation, and complement large-population coexistence criteria. The claim is local deterministic resilience only; no general global or stochastic benefit is implied.
